<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">IRVING,
Texas &#8211; October 27, 2017 &#8211; Exxon Mobil Corporation announced estimated third
quarter 2017 earnings of $4&nbsp;billion, or $0.93 per diluted share, compared
with $2.7&nbsp;billion a year earlier as commodity prices improved and
performance in the Upstream and Downstream strengthened. Impacts related to
Hurricane Harvey reduced earnings by an estimated 4&nbsp;cents per share.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:2.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:2.0pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&#8220;A 50&nbsp;percent
increase in earnings through solid business performance and higher commodity
prices is a step forward in our plan to grow profitability,&#8221; said Darren Woods,
chairman and chief executive officer. &#8220;For the fourth-consecutive quarter, we
generated cash flow from operations and asset sales that more than covered our
dividends and net investments in the business.&#8221;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:2.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:2.0pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:2.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:2.0pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Upstream
earnings rose to $1.6 billion as commodity prices increased. Building on its
recent success in deepwater exploration, such as the Turbot discovery in
Guyana, ExxonMobil added 12&nbsp;offshore blocks in Brazil, capturing acreage
with high resource potential and competitive fiscal terms. </font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:2.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:2.0pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:2.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:2.0pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Downstream
results increased to $1.5 billion, despite Hurricane Harvey impacts and the
absence of favorable asset management gains of $380&nbsp;million in the prior
year from the sale of Canadian retail assets. These results were achieved as
the company worked quickly to safely bring refineries back online following the
storm and to restore product supplies. </font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-top:12.0pt;"><sup><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><i><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">1</font></i></font></sup><font color=black face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><i><font color=black face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Includes
additions to property, plant and equipment and net investments / advances</font></i></font></p>

  </td>
 <td valign=top width=93% style="border:none;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="font-size:11.0pt;">During the quarter, ExxonMobil announced it
  added 22,000&nbsp;acres since May to its Permian Basin portfolio through a
  series of acquisitions and acreage trades.&#160; Located in the Delaware and
  Midland Basins, the new acreage adds over 400&nbsp;million oil&#8209;equivalent
  barrels to the company&#8217;s existing Permian Basin resource base of 6&nbsp;billion
  oil&#8209;equivalent barrels. </font></p>
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 <td width=4% style="border:none;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;"><p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p></td>
 </tr>

  <td valign=top width=3% style="border:none;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">

  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><b><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="font-size:11.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;text-transform:uppercase;">&#8226;</font></b></p>
  </td>
 <td valign=top width=93% style="border:none;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="font-size:11.0pt;">ExxonMobil completed the acquisition of one
  of the world&#8217;s largest aromatics facilities, located in Singapore, from
  Jurong Aromatics Corporation Pte Ltd. The acquisition will provide
  operational and logistical synergies between the plant and ExxonMobil&#8217;s
  integrated refining and petrochemical complex, as well as increase ExxonMobil
  Singapore&#8217;s aromatics production to over 3.5 million metric tons per year.&#160; </font></p>
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=center style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;mso-border-shadow:yes;mso-padding-alt:31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt;text-align:center;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif style="border:none;display:none;mso-bidi-font-family:Times New Roman;mso-fareast-font-family:Calibri;mso-hide:all;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%;">&lt;/BCLPAGE&gt;</font></font><font face=Calibri,sans-serif style="border:none;mso-bidi-font-family:Times New Roman;mso-fareast-font-family:Calibri;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%;">2</DIV>

<DIV bclHeader>


<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;mso-border-shadow:yes;mso-line-height-rule:exactly;mso-padding-alt:31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt;mso-pagination:widow-orphan no-line-numbers;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:.7pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:12.0pt;"><b><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;layout-grid-mode:line;line-height:115%;">Third Quarter 2017 vs. Third Quarter 2016</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Upstream earnings were $1.6&nbsp;billion in
the third quarter of 2017, up $947&nbsp;million from the third quarter of 2016.
Higher liquids and gas realizations increased earnings by $860&nbsp;million.
Higher volume and mix effects increased earnings by $20&nbsp;million. All other
items increased earnings by $70&nbsp;million as lower expenses were partly
offset by unfavorable foreign exchange effects. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">On an oil&#8209;equivalent basis, production
increased 2&nbsp;percent from the third quarter of 2016. Liquids production
totaled 2.3&nbsp;million barrels per day, up 69,000&nbsp;barrels per day as
lower downtime and higher project volumes were partly offset by field decline. Natural
gas production was 9.6&nbsp;billion cubic feet per day, down 16&nbsp;million
cubic feet per day from 2016 as field decline and lower demand were partly
offset by project ramp&#8209;up, primarily in Australia, and work programs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">U.S. Upstream results were a loss of
$238&nbsp;million in the third quarter of 2017, compared to a loss of
$477&nbsp;million in the third quarter of 2016. Non&#8209;U.S. Upstream
earnings were $1.8&nbsp;billion, up</font><font color=red face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;"> </font><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">$708&nbsp;million
from the prior year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Downstream earnings were $1.5&nbsp;billion,
up $303&nbsp;million from the third quarter of 2016. Higher refining margins
increased earnings by $1&nbsp;billion. Volume and mix effects decreased
earnings by $160&nbsp;million. All other items decreased earnings by $550&nbsp;million,
reflecting the absence of favorable asset management gains of $380&nbsp;million
in the prior year from the sale of Canadian retail assets and higher expenses
related to Hurricane Harvey. Petroleum product sales of 5.5&nbsp;million barrels
per day were 43,000&nbsp;barrels per day lower than last year&#8217;s third quarter. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Earnings from the U.S. Downstream were $391&nbsp;million,
up $166 million from the third quarter of 2016. Non&#8209;U.S. Downstream
earnings of $1.1&nbsp;billion were $137&nbsp;million higher than prior year. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Chemical earnings of $1.1&nbsp;billion were $79&nbsp;million
lower than the third quarter of 2016. Weaker margins decreased earnings by $200&nbsp;million.
Volume and mix effects increased earnings by $120&nbsp;million. Third quarter
prime product sales of 6.4&nbsp;million metric tons&nbsp;were 313,000&nbsp;metric
tons or 5&nbsp;percent higher than the prior year, despite Hurricane Harvey
impacts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">U.S. Chemical earnings of $403 million were
$31 million lower than the third quarter of 2016. Non&#8209;U.S. Chemical
earnings of $689&nbsp;million were $48&nbsp;million lower than prior year. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Corporate and financing expenses were $221 million
for the third quarter of 2017, down $149&nbsp;million from the third quarter of
2016 mainly due to favorable impacts from the resolution of long&#8209;standing
tax items.</font></p>

<p align=center style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;mso-border-shadow:yes;mso-padding-alt:31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt;text-align:center;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif style="border:none;display:none;mso-bidi-font-family:Times New Roman;mso-fareast-font-family:Calibri;mso-hide:all;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%;">&lt;/BCLPAGE&gt;</font></font><font face=Calibri,sans-serif style="border:none;mso-bidi-font-family:Times New Roman;mso-fareast-font-family:Calibri;"><font face=Calibri,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%;">3</DIV>
</DIV><HR noshade STYLE="page-break-after: always" align="center" width="100%" size=2><a name="page_4"></a><DIV bclPageBorder STYLE="PADDING-TOP: 0.3in; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0.3in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0.5in; PADDING-LEFT: 0.5in">

<DIV bclHeader>


<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;mso-border-shadow:yes;mso-line-height-rule:exactly;mso-padding-alt:31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt;mso-pagination:widow-orphan no-line-numbers;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:.7pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:12.0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">First
Nine Months 2017 vs. First Nine Months 2016</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Upstream earnings were $5&nbsp;billion, up $4.2&nbsp;billion
from 2016. Higher realizations increased earnings by $4.1&nbsp;billion. Unfavorable
volume and mix effects decreased earnings by $300&nbsp;million. All other items
increased earnings by $380&nbsp;million, primarily due to lower expenses partly
offset by unfavorable tax items in the current year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">On an oil&#8209;equivalent basis, production
of 4&nbsp;million barrels per day was down 1&nbsp;percent compared to 2016.
Liquids production of 2.3&nbsp;million barrels per day decreased 65,000&nbsp;barrels
per day as field decline and lower entitlements were partly offset by increased
project volumes and work programs. Natural gas production of 10.1&nbsp;billion
cubic feet per day increased 106&nbsp;million cubic feet per day from 2016 as
project ramp&#8209;up, primarily in Australia, was partly offset by field
decline.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;text-decoration:none;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">U.S. Upstream results were a loss of
$439&nbsp;million in 2017, compared to a loss of $1.8 billion in 2016. Earnings
outside the U.S. were $5.4&nbsp;billion, up $2.8&nbsp;billion from the prior
year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Downstream earnings of $4&nbsp;billion
increased $1.1&nbsp;billion from 2016. Stronger refining and marketing margins
increased earnings by $1.3&nbsp;billion, while volume and mix effects increased
earnings by $110 million. All other items decreased earnings by
$290&nbsp;million, mainly reflecting the absence of the Canadian retail assets
sale. Petroleum product sales of 5.5&nbsp;million barrels per day were 26,000&nbsp;barrels
per day higher than 2016. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">U.S. Downstream earnings were $1&nbsp;billion,
an increase of $206&nbsp;million from 2016. Non&#8209;U.S. Downstream earnings
were $3&nbsp;billion, up $867&nbsp;million from the prior year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Chemical earnings of $3.2 billion decreased $495&nbsp;million
from 2016. Weaker margins decreased earnings by $320&nbsp;million. Volume and
mix effects increased earnings by $70&nbsp;million. All other items decreased
earnings by $250&nbsp;million, primarily due to higher expenses from increased
turnaround activity and new business growth. Prime product sales of 18.6&nbsp;million
metric tons were up 22,000&nbsp;metric tons from the first nine months of 2016.
</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">U.S. Chemical earnings were $1.4&nbsp;billion,
down $111&nbsp;million from 2016. Non&#8209;U.S. Chemical earnings of $1.8&nbsp;billion
were $384&nbsp;million lower than prior year. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Corporate and financing expenses were $954 million
in 2017 compared to $1.4 billion in 2016, with the decrease mainly due to favorable
impacts from the resolution of long&#8209;standing tax items.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">During the first nine months of 2017, Exxon
Mobil Corporation purchased 6&nbsp;million shares of its common stock for the
treasury at a gross cost of $496&nbsp;million. These shares were acquired to
offset dilution in conjunction with the company&#8217;s benefit plans and programs.
The corporation will continue to acquire shares to offset dilution in
conjunction with its benefit plans and programs, but does not currently plan on
making purchases to reduce shares outstanding. The company also issued a
combined 96 million shares of common stock during the first quarter to complete
the acquisition of InterOil Corporation and the acquisition of entities that
own oil and gas properties located primarily in the Permian Basin. </font></p>




<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:115%;">&nbsp;</font></p>

</DIV><HR noshade STYLE="page-break-after: always" align="center" width="100%" size=2><a name="page_5"></a><DIV bclPageBorder STYLE="PADDING-TOP: 0.3in; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0.3in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0.5in; PADDING-LEFT: 0.5in">

<DIV bclHeader>


<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;mso-border-shadow:yes;mso-line-height-rule:exactly;mso-padding-alt:31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt;mso-pagination:widow-orphan no-line-numbers;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:.7pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>
<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Forward-looking
Statements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">As part of its annual planning and budgeting
cycle which is completed in the fourth quarter each year, the corporation
develops crude and natural gas price outlooks as well as estimates of future
costs and other factors necessary to complete its plan. Management&#8217;s price
outlook and other factors, including factors such as operating costs, resource
productivity, and capital efficiency, are re-assessed when facts and
circumstances warrant but no less often than annually. To the extent any
impairment testing may be required, management uses assumptions that are
reasonable in relation to these factors in developing estimates of future cash
flows. An asset group would be impaired if its estimated undiscounted cash
flows were less than the asset&#8217;s carrying value, and impairment would be
measured by the amount by which the carrying value exceeds fair value.
Development of future undiscounted cash flow estimates requires significant
management judgment, particularly in cases where an asset&#8217;s life is expected to
extend decades into the future, and an important component of the estimate is
management&#8217;s outlook on prices and other factors as noted above.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">The corporation has identified emerging
trends such as increasing estimates of available natural gas supplies and
ongoing reductions in costs of supply for natural gas. In the fourth quarter of
2017, the corporation will incorporate the impacts of these trends and the
resulting lower price outlook in its annual planning and budgeting cycle. Once
complete, the corporation expects to perform an impairment assessment for its
North American natural gas asset groups utilizing the information developed as
part of the planning and budgeting process. It is not practicable at this time
to estimate the impact these trends would have on the undiscounted cash flows
for individual asset groups or any resulting impairment charges. However these
trends are likely to place the corporation&#8217;s North American natural gas asset
groups at risk for potential impairment.&#160; The corporation will complete its
analysis of relevant factors as discussed above and perform any necessary impairment
testing in connection with the preparation of the corporation&#8217;s year&#8209;end
financial statements for inclusion in its 2017 Form 10&#8209;K.</font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif style="border:none;"><i><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:11.0pt;">Statements

exploration and development efforts; changes in law or government regulation,
including tax and environmental requirements; the impact of fiscal and
commercial terms and outcome of commercial negotiations; the results of research
programs; changes in technical or operating conditions; actions of competitors;
and other factors discussed under the heading &quot;Factors Affecting Future
Results&quot; in the &#8220;Investors&#8221; section of our website and in Item 1A of
ExxonMobil's 2016 Form 10&#8209;K. We assume no duty to update these statements
